title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A qualifier is not a parent
summary: A supertype written Outer.Inner was filed under both names, so a type of the workspace sharing a name with a framework one claimed its children. On a real Android project, 165 types were over counted by 2020 implementations in total.

highlights.title: 96 became 3, and 3 was right
highlights.description: One Java class extending RecyclerView.ViewHolder was filed under its own name, became its own descendant, and dragged 92 classes into three unrelated counts.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A supertype written Outer.Inner names one parent, Inner. Both segments used to enter the hierarchy, so a nested interface called View claimed the 51 classes that extend android's View, and a nested ViewHolder claimed 92.

An explicit import decides what a simple name means, which is what Kotlin does. Only types declared in the workspace were consulted, so importing a class from a library contradicted nothing and the local namesake took the credit.
A type is no longer its own subtype, and the qualifier still counts for spotting a framework ancestor, so nothing new is reported as unused.
